terra.problem: “That's everybody” extends the action beyond those buying and selling, the people the text specifies.
The raccoon adds an unestablished animal to Papa Dorin's world, where he lives alone.
“Then” imposes an order on driving people out and overturning things, and the text does not say nobody received a gentle request.
The claim that nothing in that corner was left as Jesus found it goes beyond the tables and seats the text identifies.
“The whole setup” extends what was overturned beyond the tables and seats specified in the text.
The last two sentences are generic commentary on finding the answer rather than an explanation in Papa Dorin's voice.
“The room had just been cleared out” overstates the action: Jesus drove out those buying and selling, not everyone present.
“Tough crowd” makes the chief priests and scribes the target of the joke.
Jesus says He hears what the children are saying, but the text does not say He heard every word.
“The littlest voices in the room” suggests infants were present and speaking there. The text mentions children shouting, but does not say infants were present.
“Wrong town” calls the baker's answer wrong, which Papa Dorin must not do.
“That's where the night happens” is flat filler and adds nothing to the explanation.
The text says the tree had nothing except leaves, not that it was full of leaves or looked as though it should have fruit.
“Expecting something” assigns Jesus an expectation the text does not state.
The short-story joke makes the way the Scripture story is written the joke.
“Where we just were” places Papa Dorin at the temple during the Bible event.
The explanation repeats the verse and ends with a generic observation about its position, without adding a meaningful explanation.
